is a highsec mining & industry alliance. We mine the rock, refine the rock, build with the rock, and sell the thing.
He weeps. We do not care.

Some of us have been flying since before half these ships existed. Some joined this week and are still working out which laser goes where. The rock does not care how long you have played, and neither do we. Same buyback, same fleet, same shot at the wall, from your first hour.
A corp is just the people who keep showing up, and this many of us keep showing up. Almost every one of us got here the same way:
The Dropouts founded the alliance and still haul the most rock in it. Corps join
You point the laser. The rock does not consent. This is the part you already love.
The buyback gathers it and the minerals come out. No hauling to Jita like it's 1843.
Our own minerals, our own blueprints. The new frontier, and the big margins live here.
Finished goods at a margin. ISK appears. A goblin, somewhere, feels useful.
Better refine, more yield, our own everything. The final goblin form. Coming this season.

— damn near double, measured. These aren't vibes; this is the live Mining Burst readout:
Mine it, dump it in the buyback, get paid
. The math is already done and the rate is already fair. Hauling is for people without a corp.
Near-zero corp tax — we fund the dynasty on the buyback margin, not your wallet.
Explode in the field? We hand you a fresh hull out of the Orca's bay and you're back on the rock in minutes.
The horror of solo mining ends here.

that a recruiter actually reviews, then hands you a one time claim code. Clean funnel, zero spam.

Gather round. The corp keeps a wall of honors, and every one of them is now earnable on stated terms. No vague vibes, no handouts. Real goals. Worthy ones.
Earned over time, granted at the CEO's hand. These you do not grind, you become.
The highest honor we bestow upon an industrialist, the pilot whose work IS the foundation. Without them there is no fleet, no empire.

· be the rare goblin the dynasty is visibly built on: sustained contribution across mining, buyback, and corp building over a year or more, the kind everyone already knows the name of. Granted by the CEO. There will only ever be a few.
Granted to those who do not merely mine, but build. For vision, output, and turning raw rock into the lifeblood of the corp.
· run the full chain: manufacture from corp minerals and put 1B ISK or more of finished goods into the corp or the market. You do not just feed the machine, you ARE the machine.
Patron Saint of the New Goblin
For patiently teaching new pilots the ropes, asking nothing in return. Where others recruit, this one raises.
· mentor new goblins such that 3 or more of your students are still here after 30 days. Measured in people who stayed, not hours spent. Granted by the CEO on the evidence.
You should see the other guy.
· stand and fight when it counts: take a real scrap (gank defense, a duel, holding the belt) and walk away with the killmail or the war story to show for it. Granted by the CEO.
Fifty ops. Some pilots have a personality; this one has an attendance record the belt itself respects. Alliances rose and died while this goblin was mid rotation.
· attend 50 settled fleet ops on the drop ledger. Tracked automatically, granted on the numbers. No shortcuts, no substitute for showing up.
The crown is not a hat, it is a job. Twenty five paydays happened because this goblin undocked first and everyone else got to just mine.
· command 25 settled fleet ops: take the crown, call the rock, finish the fleet, and pay every goblin. The ledger remembers who ran the show.
Hard numbers. Hit the bar, get the medal.
Completed their first joint extraction with the crew. Every dynasty is built one full hold at a time. This was theirs.
· complete one mining op with the fleet and deliver that haul to the buyback. Your welcome to the family.
Sat through the whole Academy and passed every quiz. Knows the doctrine, the workflow, and where the checks come from. Officially a trained goblin, no longer a liability.
· complete all six modules of the BONK Academy in the member portal, quizzes and all. One click from the moment you finish.
Clocks in, drops, gets paid, comes back. The rock fears routine more than it fears lasers.
· attend 10 settled fleet ops. Tracked automatically. The first step on the road to The Long Haul.
One million cubic meters through the ledger. Cities have been built with less material and worse attitude.
· haul a lifetime total of 1,000,000 m³ of rock and ice, fleet drops and accepted contracts combined. The career page counts it for you.
Fifty recorded hours in the belt. The rocks started the relationship; this goblin made it official.
· put in 50 hours of recorded belt time, first drop to last, op after op. We said rocks over therapy. You took it as a vow.
Fed the dynasty with their own hands. No hoarding, no lonely Jita runs. They send the ore in, take the fair payout, and the whole machine eats because of it.
· deliver a lifetime total of 1,000,000,000 ISK of ore and ice through the corp buyback.
Where others mine, this one multiplies. Led ten lost souls out of the cold dark and into the fold.
· recruit 10 pilots who join both the Discord and the corp.
For one entire month, no belt was safe and no goblin out mined them. The rocks saw this one undock and quietly updated their wills.
· finish a calendar month as the corp's number one miner by the in-game mining ledger.
Thirty days. Zero dead barges. Disciplined, unbothered, and quietly getting rich while the reckless feed the gankers.
· go 30 straight days without losing a mining ship. We check the kill log. It sees all.
Ninety days in and still here. Came for the boosts, stayed for the brotherhood, discovered they cannot leave.
· reach 90 days in the corp. You stayed. We noticed. It is permanent now.
Every haul carries a tip to the boss, and this one tipped harder than anyone. Fat wallet, open hand, and the whole fleet knows it.
· finish a calendar month having tipped the fleet bosses more ISK than any other goblin. The default tip is 10 percent, so just keep dropping.
Not a goblin, but family all the same. The allied pilot who out-hauled every other friend of the corp this month. Corp medals are for corp goblins; this one is for our friends.
Finish a calendar month as the top Friend of the Rock on the fleet ledger. Roll with a BONK fleet, drop your ore, out-haul the other friends.
Seventeen honors. Every one earnable, none handed out. Pick your goal and make the ore flow toward it.

The Sacred Choreography of Rock Acquisition
Module 2 · How We Run A Fleet

A fleet is what happens when a bunch of goblins agree to be in the same place and point their lasers at the same field of rocks at the same time, which sounds simple and is somehow the thing people mess up most. So here is the choreography. Learn it once and never ask in fleet again.
Step one. Get in the fleet.

The boosts, which are the reason you make real money instead of peasant money, only reach people who are actually IN the fleet. If you are mining next to the fleet but not in it, you are just a stranger nearby doing manual labor for free, like a raccoon going through the neighbor's trash. Be in the fleet.

We move as one. Together is faster, together is safer, and together means when something goes wrong we all warp out looking like professionals instead of one guy exploding alone while everyone watches.
Step three. Stay within 40km of the Orca.

The Orca is the big ship in the middle projecting an invisible bubble of pure yield around itself, and inside that bubble you mine roughly 83% faster. Eighty three percent. The moment you drift outside 40km, that bubble does nothing and your yield quietly collapses to the sad numbers of a man mining alone. Stay in the bubble. Get rich.

Position yourself so you can reach a fat field of rocks WHILE you are pointed at some faraway celestial. You stay pointed at the door the whole time. A goblin who mines aligned dies of old age. A goblin who mines sideways dies on a Tuesday.
Step five. When your hold is full, you do TWO things at once, every time, as one habit: you jetcan the ore, AND you log it in the ledger.

These are not separate tasks. Jetcan and log. Jetcan and log. Burn it in. Before the op even starts, open the Fleet Drop Ledger at bonkeve.com/fleet, punch in the fleet password and your pilot name, and leave it open. Then when your hold fills: jettison the ore into a can, and in the same breath select that ore with Ctrl+A, copy with Ctrl+C, paste it into the ledger, and hit Drop. The ledger now knows exactly what you dropped and you are on record to get paid for every unit.
Step six. The robots and the Orca handle the rest.

You do not compress your own ore. A little robot called the MTU reels your cans in automatically, like a Roomba for space rocks, and the Orca crushes the whole pile down when its hold is full and the grid is clear. You just keep mining, keep jetcanning, keep logging.
Step seven. The ore goes home, and Fear writes the checks.
And because you logged every drop, your check is exactly right, and nobody can argue about it.

Seven Rules That Cost Us A Lot To Learn

This is the most important module in the entire Academy. Every one of these seven rules was paid for. Not with theory. With ships. Real ones. Expensive ones. We learned them the hard way so you do not have to. In return you have to read seven bullet points. Deal.

None of these rules are obvious. That is the trap. Every one is the exact opposite of what your gut will scream at you in the moment. Your gut is going to get you killed. Follow the rules instead of the gut.

The instant you shoot, point, web, or send a drone at a hostile in highsec, you sign a permission slip that turns off your protection. That is a limited engagement. Our safety is not our guns. It is CONCORD, the space police, who delete anyone who attacks us, but only if we did not throw the first punch.
Your weapon is the warp drive. Your shield is CONCORD.
You do not have guns. Act like it.
Rule 2. Never help a corpmate who is already in a fight.

This one feels heroic and heroism is a trap. Rush in to rep him or send drones and you flag YOURSELF as a legal target too. You did not save him, you doubled the killmail. We have watched one loss become four this exact way.
Disengage, warp out, regroup, we reship the guy.
Rule 3. The Orca's Core stays down.

When the Orca turns on its Industrial Core it becomes a building. It cannot move, cannot warp, it is a very expensive statue. The boosts work fine without it, so the Core only comes up for one quick compress cycle when the hold is full and the grid is clear, then straight back down.
Rule 4. Watch local, but be a human about it.

You do not panic and dock up every time one neutral shows up. But a combat ship on the field, someone burning at you, a name you know is trouble? You are already aligned, so you just warp. Calmly. Use your eyes and use your head.
Rule 5. Your barge drones are for killing rats, not people.

Here is the trap: five barges see one 'lone' hostile and think 'we outnumber him.' The second your drones touch him, all five of you are flagged, and that lone hostile always has friends one jump away who were counting on exactly this. It is bait. It is always bait. The miners never fight.

Yes, again. Position so you can reach the rocks while holding an align off grid, so when trouble lands you are already leaving instead of sitting there ten agonizing seconds spooling your warp drive. Mine pointed at the door. Every time.

We have paid before, and we got shot anyway, every time, because a person who ambushes you for money is not bound by a strong code of honor. A ransom is a donation to the man about to kill you. Keep your wallet shut. We reship our own.

Core down, aligned out, local watched, nobody engages, nobody plays hero.

The whole job, in one loop

Mine rocks. Tell the ledger what you mined. Get paid your exact share when the op ends. This walkthrough shows the full loop once, including the part inside EVE. Thirty seconds, then you never think about it again.
Before the op: someone found this rock
Fleet command picks the spot with Radar, our belt scanner. You just fly where the fleet flies. If you ever want to scout your own, the Radar tool on the toolbelt knows every belt in New Eden.
Your ore is priced the moment you drop it

This strip is the op at a glance: the system the fleet is in right now, what we are mining, who runs it, and the buyback cut. The ledger values every rock at live Jita prices, the market where everything actually sells. No haggling, no spreadsheets, the math is already done.
In EVE: select what you mined
Open your ore hold or the can you filled. Click one stack, then Ctrl+A grabs them all. Partial stacks are fine. This is just selecting, nothing moves yet.

With the stacks selected, Ctrl+C copies them as text. Do this BEFORE you jettison or compress, while the ore is still in front of you. Then right click and Jettison for the hauler like normal. Copy first, dump second. That order is the whole trick.
Tell the ledger who you are
Pick the pilot the ISK should land on. Flying alts? Add each one once with + alt and tap between them. Every drop pays the name it was dropped under.
Click the box, Ctrl+V, hit Drop. The ledger reads the stacks, prices them, and adds them to your tab. Do this every time your hold fills. It becomes muscle memory by the second can.
The lazy way, once you have a rhythm
Grinding one ore all night? After the first drop it becomes a chip up here. Dial the number, tap drop, back to the belt. Chips reset each op so Monday's ice never haunts Thursday's Veldspar.
Scout the next rock before you undock

See a fat anomaly in the Agency window? Type the system here. The scout draws the route from where the fleet sits right now, checks every system on the way plus the destination's neighbors against the last hour of kills, and hands down a verdict. Command can set the fleet location or announce the op there in one tap.

If your drop shows here, you are getting paid for it, and the receipt lives on your portal career page forever. If it is not on the feed, the ledger never saw it, and unlogged ore is charity. Check the feed, then go fill another hold.
Tips, payday, and you are done

Corp norm is a 10 percent tip to the fleet boss and it is already set; tap none to opt out, nobody is watching. When the op wraps, command runs the payout and your exact cut lands in your wallet. That is the loop: copy, paste, drop, get paid. Welcome to organized violence against geology.
